Welcome toRemoving the Partition

A gas held in half a box — take the partition out and count.

How would you like to begin?

Listen to the intro

About: an ideal gas spreading into the empty half of a box, and the left–right macrostate

Source

Concept
Microstates and macrostates of N non-interacting molecules in a box of length L and height L/2; the entropy S = kB ln Ω of the macrostate labelled by nL, the number of molecules in the left half.
Serves
Explaining how often the whole gas is found back in the left half, and how far nL/N wanders, for N from 2 to 10 000.
Inquiry
Six questions and a closing summary card. Each question asks for a run at a chosen N, then a reading of the trace, the nL/N or S/kB readout, or the count of looks that find every molecule on the left. A look is taken once every crossing time τ after removal.
Misconception
The choices probe what the second law says about an isolated gas of a few molecules and of many.

Pedagogy principles applied

Commit, then checkEach question asks for a committed choice. The student then runs the gas and checks the answer in the sim; each choice has its own feedback.
Staged readoutsThe Readouts panel sits below the controls. Only the readouts the current card asks about are shown; all six appear in free exploration.
Operational quantitiesnL, nL/N, S/kB and the look counts are counted from the simulated molecules themselves. S/kB = ln N! − ln nL! − ln(N − nL)! is computed from the log-gamma function.
Honest scalingThe plot title states that the motion is slowed (τ = 0.5 s on screen at 1×, shorter at the faster Speed settings) and that the dots are enlarged. Each speed is drawn from the 2-D Maxwell distribution and never changes, so the energy of the gas stays constant.
Stable axes, no hint linesThe graph runs from 0 to 1 over a fixed 40τ window. No reference line or expected value is drawn, so the student finds where the trace settles.
Loud state changeA solid grey partition is drawn while it is in. Once it is removed, a faint dashed line marks where it stood.
Removing the Partition
Isolated ideal gas in a box (motion slowed: τ = 0.5 s on screen, dots enlarged)
Fraction in the left half, nL/N, against time since removal

Guided Inquiry

1 · Removing the partition

Keep N = 10 000, press Remove partition, and watch the trace and the readout of nL/N for about ten seconds. What does the fraction of the molecules in the left half do?

2 · Two molecules

Set N = 2, press Remove partition, and let it run until the readout shows 100 looks, which takes about 50 s (about 13 s with Speed set to 4×). What fraction of the looks find both molecules in the left half?

3 · The entropy of a return

Keep N = 2 and watch the S/kB readout, the entropy of the left–right macrostate measured from its value before the partition was removed. What does it read each time the trace touches 1, with both molecules in the left half?

4 · Four molecules

Set N = 4, press Remove partition, and let it run to 200 looks, about 100 s (25 s with Speed set to 4×). What fraction of the looks now find every molecule in the left half?

5 · Twenty molecules

Set N = 20, press Remove partition, and let it run for a few minutes, with Speed set to 4×, watching the count of looks that find every molecule on the left. How often would a look find all twenty in the left half?

6 · How far the fraction wanders

Set N = 100, press Remove partition, and watch the trace and the readout of nL/N for about 20 s after the trace has settled. Then set N = 10 000 and do the same. How does the wander of nL/N about one half change?

7 · The second law as counting

Once the partition is out, each molecule is equally likely to be in either half. The chance that a look finds all N back on the left is 2−N: one in four for 2 molecules, once in six days for 20, and for a mole of gas never in the age of the universe.

So the entropy S = kB ln Ω of the left–right macrostate can fall, but a noticeable fall becomes overwhelmingly unlikely as N grows, and nL/N wanders about one half by only 1/(2√N). The second law is a statement about likelihood that becomes a certainty for large N.

Removing the Partition

✦Learn this with the AI tutor

01

At a glance

N molecules start in the left half of a box, held there by a partition. When the partition is removed they spread out, and the sim shows where they are with a trace, a count of looks and an entropy readout. N runs from 2 to 10 000, so a handful of molecules and a large gas can be compared.

What you'll learn

  • How the chance of finding all N molecules back on the left depends on N.
  • What the S/kB readout counts.
  • How the fraction nL/N behaves for a few molecules and for many.
  • What the second law says about an isolated gas of a few molecules and of many.
The box as the sim draws it, length L and height L/2, with the partition in.

What's on screen

  • Cyan dots are the molecules, drawn larger than life. The grey bar is the partition; once it is out, a faint dashed line marks where it stood.
  • Cyan trace (below the box) is the fraction nL/N of molecules in the left half, against the time since removal in units of τ. Its axis is fixed from 0 to 1 over a 40τ window.
  • Readouts: N, nL, nL/N, S/kB, the number of looks, and how many looks found all N on the left.
See itRemove the partition at your current N. Watch for: the dots leaving the left half, and the trace starting from 1 at the left edge of the graph.

Fixed: the molecules are points that bounce off the walls of the box and never collide with one another. Each keeps the speed it was given, drawn from the 2-D Maxwell distribution with a mean of L per τ, and a bounce sends it off in a random direction. Looks start counting at the removal.

03

Finding all N molecules on the left has chance 2−N

Once the gas has spread, the molecules move independently and each is equally likely to be found in either half. A look counts the molecules in the left half at one instant. Of the 2N equally likely left–right placements, exactly one has every molecule on the left.

Notes (4.1) with p = q = 1/2 and n = N. The notes’ n is the sim’s nL.

For N = 2 the four placements are LL, LR, RL and RR, so a look finds both on the left with chance 1/4. For N = 4 it is 1/16. For N = 20 it is 1/1 048 576, about one look in a million: at one look per 0.5 s that is one return in about 6.1 days.

See itRemove the partition with N = 2. Watch for: the trace jumping between 0, 0.5 and 1, and the count of looks with all N on the left rising on about one look in four.
04

S/kB counts the placements of the macrostate the gas is in

The readout is ln Ω for the left–right macrostate the gas is in now, the one labelled by nL. Ω is the number of ways of choosing which molecules are on the left. It does not count all 2N placements at once.

Notes (4.26) and (4.1): S = kB ln Ω, with the binomial coefficient for Ω.

With the partition in, every molecule is on the left, Ω = 1 and the readout is 0.00, the value it is measured from. For N = 2, one molecule in each half is two placements, LR and RL, so it reads ln 2 = 0.69. For N = 4 the five macrostates hold 1, 4, 6, 4 and 1 of the 16 placements. Both ends, nL = 0 and nL = N, are a single placement and read 0.00.

N = 4. Bars show Ω; the last row is what the readout shows.
See itRemove the partition with N = 4. Watch for: the readout reading 1.79 when two molecules are on each side, 1.39 when the split is one and three, and 0.00 when all four are on one side.
05

A fall in entropy is allowed, and for many molecules absurdly rare

Nothing in the motion forbids a return. The molecules keep crossing, and whenever all N are on the left again the readout is back at 0.00. For N = 2 that is a fall of 0.69 and happens on about one look in four. For N = 20 the readout stays below, and mostly close to, its largest value ln C(20, 10) = 12.13, and a return would be a fall to 0.00, on about one look in a million.

The notes make the same point (p. 106): nothing forbids the entropy of an isolated system from decreasing, and a decrease by a measurable amount is merely overwhelmingly unlikely. From N = 2 to N = 20 the chance falls by 218 = 262 144 times; at N = 10 it is 1/1 024. A count of zero after minutes at N = 20 therefore means rare, not forbidden.

See itRemove the partition with N = 20. Watch for: S/kB staying between about 10 and 12 while the count of looks with all N on the left stays at zero.
06

The fraction wanders by 1/(2√N)

With p = q = 1/2 the count nL has mean N/2 and standard deviation √N/2 (notes, 4.2–4.3). The trace draws the fraction nL/N, so its spread is σn/N, half the notes’ relative width 1/√N (4.4), because the mean fraction is 1/2.

The spread in the count grows as √N; the spread in the fraction falls as 1/√N.

At N = 100 the spread in nL is 5 and the fraction wanders by ±0.050. At N = 10 000 the spread is 50 and the wander is ±0.005. A hundredfold more molecules makes the spread in the count ten times larger and the wander of the fraction ten times smaller, not a hundred.

One standard deviation of nL/N at the nine settings of N.
See itRemove the partition with N = 100 (set for this demo). Watch for: the trace wandering through a band of about 0.05 either side of 0.5, and the nL readout staying within a few of 50.
07

Where it matters

  • Pressure and density. For N of the order of Avogadro’s number the fraction on one side wanders by about 10−12, so a gas’s density is a definite number rather than a flickering one (notes, p. 95).
  • The second law as counting. Removing a constraint makes more placements available, so Ω can only increase, and the gas spends almost all its time in the macrostate with the largest Ω (notes, p. 106).
  • Why you never see it happen. For a mole of gas the chance 2−N is about 10−1.8×1023 per look, so no look in the age of the universe would find the gas back in one half.
08

Summary

In one line. The sim releases N molecules into the empty half of a box and reads their spread through a trace, an entropy readout and a count of looks.

Key points

  • A look finds all N on the left with chance 2−N: 1/4 for two molecules, about 1 in 106 for twenty.
  • S/kB = ln C(N, nL) counts the placements of the current macrostate, so it can fall back to 0.00.
  • The fraction nL/N wanders by 1/(2√N): ±0.050 at N = 100, ±0.005 at N = 10 000.

Common mix-ups

  • “Once the gas is mixed, nL/N stops changing.” The molecules keep crossing both ways. At N = 10 000 the fraction keeps wandering by about ±0.005.
  • “S/kB keeps its highest value, because entropy cannot fall.” For two molecules it reads 0.00 whenever both are on the left. A fall is unlikely only when N is large.

Things to try on your own

  • With N = 2, run 100 looks and compare the count of looks with both molecules on the left with 100/4. Repeat with N = 4 and 200 looks against 200/16.
  • Compare how far the nL/N readout strays from 0.500 at N = 100 and at N = 10 000; the ratio should be about ten.
